learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the invisible force that rules the cosmos! Explore how massive bodies attract each other, how planets orbit, and how to calculate escape velocity.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: 1. Planets move in elliptical orbits. 2. A line from the sun to a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (planets move faster when closer to the sun). 3. The square of the time period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis ($T^2 \propto r^3$).

Newton realized every mass attracts every other mass. The force is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them: $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$.

Acceleration due to gravity ($g$) is maximum on the Earth's surface. It decreases if you go high up into the atmosphere (altitude), and it also decreases if you dig deep down into the Earth (depth). It is exactly zero at the center of the Earth!

The energy stored due to an object's position in a gravitational field. By convention, it is zero at infinity and negative everywhere else ($U = -G\frac{Mm}{r}$), meaning the system is bound together.

Orbital velocity is the speed needed to stay in orbit. Escape velocity is the minimum speed needed to break free from a planet's gravity forever ($v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$). For Earth, it is $11.2 \text{ km/s}$!

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Your Weight on Jupiter
fun_activity.instructions: Your mass (kg) never changes, but your weight (Force) depends on the planet's gravity. Since Jupiter's gravity is roughly 2.5 times Earth's, if you weigh 50 kg on Earth, you would feel like you weigh 125 kg on Jupiter!

exam_tips: 📌 The derivations for the variation of $g$ with height and depth are absolute must-knows for long answer questions.

📌 Be very careful with the Universal Gravitational Constant ($G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$) versus acceleration due to gravity ($g = 9.8$). $G$ is the same everywhere in the universe; $g$ changes constantly.
📌 Total energy of an orbiting satellite is negative. If the total energy becomes zero or positive, the satellite escapes the orbit.
quick_recap: ⭐ The force of gravity is the weakest of the fundamental forces of nature, but it rules the universe because it has infinite range.
⭐ Geostationary satellites orbit exactly once every 24 hours, so they appear completely stationary in the sky.
⭐ Weightlessness in a space station isn't because there is zero gravity; it's because the station and the astronaut are constantly in free-fall together!
